api::faq.faq.question: What is Listen.id?
api::faq.faq.answer: Listen.id is a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform for social media listening and media monitoring. Listen helps brands collect, analyze and visualize audience digital conversations in real-time for data-driven decision making.

api::faq.faq.question: What media sources (platforms) can be monitored?
api::faq.faq.answer: The LISTEN system performs comprehensive crawling across multiple digital channels. We monitor conversations on major social media (Instagram, X/Twitter, TikTok, Facebook,), YouTube, online news portals, and public forums.

api::faq.faq.question: Can AI Listen.id understand the slang or abbreviations of Indonesian netizens?
api::faq.faq.answer: Yes. Our Sentiment Analysis Engine is specifically designed to handle local language complexities. The system automatically processes slang, abbreviations and informal context to categorize sentiment (positive, neutral, negative) with a high degree of accuracy.

api::faq.faq.question: How do I ensure the data pulled is relevant to my brand?
api::faq.faq.answer: We use an advanced query management system with Boolean Search parameters (AND, OR, NOT). You can set keywords specifically to remove data noise and ensure search results are 100% relevant to campaign objectives.

api::faq.faq.question: Can Listen.id monitor trends and conversations in TikTok videos, Reels or Shorts?
api::faq.faq.answer: Yes, our system is designed to process multimodal content. We not only read the description/caption text, but also combine visual and audio analysis to provide a comprehensive, granular understanding of the context of the video content.

api::faq.faq.question: Can Listen.id monitor trends and conversations in TikTok videos, Reels or Shorts?
api::faq.faq.answer: Yes, our system is designed to process multimodal content. We not only read the description/caption text, but also combine visual and audio analysis to provide a comprehensive understanding of the context of the video content.

api::faq.faq.question: Does the video analysis process take longer (loading) than text?
api::faq.faq.answer: Video data processing does involve greater AI computing. However, Listen.id's infrastructure is designed to process multimodal data efficiently, so that insights from videos are still presented on your dashboard in a relatively short time (near real-time).

api::faq.faq.question: Is data from analyzed videos stored forever in the dashboard?
api::faq.faq.answer: In accordance with our privacy and data security policies, insight data and text metadata (including audio transcripts) will be retained for the duration of the subscription. However, raw video files are usually not stored on our servers for a long time in order to keep the dashboard performance fast and comply with the platform's copyright protection rules.

api::faq.faq.question: How can Listen.id help prevent PR crises?
api::faq.faq.answer: Our system works like an active shield 24/7. The Real-Time Alert System feature will immediately send instant alerts (via email) to your team if there is an abnormal spike in conversation volume or an increase in negative sentiment that has the potential to become a crisis.

Practical Guide: How to Measure Brand Sentiment with Data (Not Assumptions)
api::blog.blog.description: Complete guide article for marketers and brand managers in measuring brand sentiment objectively using data to improve creative and advertising strategies.
api::blog.blog.content:
# Practical Guide: How to Measure Brand Sentiment with Data (Not Assumptions)

Has an advertising campaign that was carefully designed, stunning visuals, and a big budget failed to captivate the audience? On the other hand, simple content actually goes viral and gets a positive response organically.

Many marketers or Brand Managers still rely on intuition or assumptions in assessing whether their products are liked. In fact, in today's digital era, every conversation on social media leaves a trail of invaluable data. This is where it is important to understand brand sentiment objectively through data.

## Why is Understanding Brand Sentiment Important?
Brand sentiment is not just counting how many people mention your brand name (mentions). More than that, sentiment measures the emotions behind the conversation. Does your audience talk about you in a positive, negative, or neutral tone?

Relying on superficial metrics (such as the number of likes or followers) without understanding the emotional context often leads to misleading marketing reports. For example, a spike in mentions may not be due to a successful product launch, but rather mass complaints about your customer service.

With accurate sentiment data, you can:

Prevent PR (Public Relations) crises before they escalate.

Finding new angles for creative campaigns.

Evaluate in real-time whether the message from your advertising is captured correctly by the target market.

### Steps to Measure Brand Sentiment Using Data

To move from assumptions to data-driven strategies, here are systematic steps you can implement:
### 1. Define comprehensive keywords
Sentiment measurement starts with collecting conversation data. Don't just track the brand name (for example, "Astra Satu Indonesia"). You should include variations your audience might use, such as:

Campaign name or official hashtag.

Spelling errors (typos) that often appear.

Names of direct competitors for comparison.

Using Boolean search (a combination of AND, OR, NOT) is very helpful in filtering data to make it relevant and discarding conversations that have nothing to do with your industry.

### 2. Collect Data Automatically (Media Monitoring)
Searching one by one (manual search) on various social media platforms is not only time consuming, but also susceptible to human bias. The volume of conversations is too large to calculate manually.

Use technological tools. Modern crawling systems can pull thousands to millions of conversations from Twitter, Instagram, TikTok, to news portals, then centralize them in one container (dashboard).

### 3. Categorization of Emotions: Positive, Negative, Neutral
Once the data is collected, it's time to assess emotions. This is where Natural Language Processing (NLP) and AI technology come into play. The system will read each text and categorize it:

Positive: Praise of the product, recommendation to others, or appreciation of service. ("This product really helps my job!")

Negative: Complaints, disappointment, or sarcasm. ("Delivery was very slow, very disappointed.")

Neutral: Brand mentions without specific emotion, usually simply sharing information or news.

Important Note: Local context greatly influences accuracy levels. Make sure your analysis tool is able to understand local slang, abbreviations or idioms (for example, Indonesian slang) so that negative sentiments disguised as sarcasm are not mistaken for positive sentiments.

### 4. Advanced Metric Analysis (Share of Voice)
Once you know the sentiment ratio, don't stop there. Compare your performance with competitors via Share of Voice (SOV).

SOV shows how big your brand's share of conversations is compared to the overall industry. If your SOV is 60% but dominated by negative sentiment, it's a strong warning that your brand is being cast in the wrong light. Conversely, an SOV of 20% with 90% positive sentiment indicates a very loyal user community.
